learningObjective: Explain the sources of the very different timings between a single-run measurement and the amortized mean of a many-run loop, and describe a correct benchmarking discipline.

canonicalClaims.claim: First-run kernel timings on CUDA include one-time initialization costs (cuBLAS handle setup, algorithm heuristics/autotune, lazy kernel loading, cache priming); a correct benchmark warms up a few iterations, then times a batch of iterations and reports a robust statistic like median.
conditions: The library in use has lazy initialization (cuBLAS/cuDNN/Triton typical behavior).
The benchmark environment is otherwise steady (no thermal throttling within the measurement window).
nonImplications: Does not imply that the first-run cost is a bug — it is expected behavior.
Does not imply that mean is always the correct reporting statistic; percentile-based reporting captures tail behavior better.

misconceptions.claim: `start.elapsed_time(end)` returns the duration of only the last operation before `end`, so dividing by 100 is meaningless.
misconceptions.whyWrong: `elapsed_time` returns the wall time between the two recorded events; if 100 ops are between them, dividing by 100 gives per-op mean.

misconceptions.claim: GPU caches tensor results across launches; the 2nd through 100th runs are 'free' because the answer is cached.
misconceptions.whyWrong: GPUs do not cache computation results; each launch recomputes from inputs.

misconceptions.claim: PyTorch invokes `torch.compile` automatically after several iterations, so a hot loop is measuring a compiled kernel.
misconceptions.whyWrong: `torch.compile` is opt-in; a plain matmul loop runs the eager cuBLAS matmul every iteration.

misconceptions.claim: First-run cost is proportional to input size, so smaller inputs eliminate it.
misconceptions.whyWrong: First-run overhead is dominated by initialization and heuristics, largely independent of input size.

implementationFacts: cuBLAS handle initialization on first use in a process
cuBLAS/cuDNN heuristic algorithm selection on first observed shape
Kernel binary lazy loading (increases on first invocation)
performanceScenarios: In serving benchmarks, cold-start latency is a real product metric; separately reporting cold (first) and hot (steady-state) latencies is standard practice.
